market_story: Coal min-load: a committed ERCOT coal plant's first MW is not cheap - the real fleet anchors its RT curve at ~$15-17/MWh (measured TPO-Price1 p50), a shallow concession below full SRMC that reflects mine-mouth/take-or-pay fuel economics, not a $4.50 VOM-only give-away; the block's must-run behaviour is carried by the two commitment floors, so the bid's only job is the merit order. Coal capability: the fleet offers what it declares to ERCOT (COP HSL), not a statistical availability estimate - and a destroyed unit (Martin Lake 1) does not come back because a class-mean rescale needs its capacity. The remaining coal-vs-gas over-run above min-load is the open root-cause lane (gas-side ranking), not bought back by re-tuning the retired estimate.
